results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester) with Schedule §1.1 (shipment from Supplier's plant). It explains that this changes whether Verdane is late for the cancellation and cover remedies, shifts risk of transit loss to Harlow, and triggers early invoicing.

The fix adds an order-of-precedence clause making the MSA prevail. It also conforms Schedule §1.1 and the related risk, title, inspection and lateness sections to delivery at Harlow's Rochester facility.

Issue 2 contrasts MSA §4.3 (all housings and similar components worldwide) with Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 (Series 7 only, U.S. only). It explains that Harlow is locked in worldwide for other products and recommends limiting exclusivity to Series 7 Housings in the United States.

Issue 6 covers both points. It notes Verdane may assign freely, including to a competitor or thinly capitalized entity, while Harlow needs consent. It flags the supply and confidential-specifications risk and recommends Harlow's consent, or at minimum a termination right and exclusivity release on assignment or change of control.

Issue 1 explains that Amendment §2.1 and §2.2 remove gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the cap exclusions. It recommends Amendment No. 2 restore the original §11.2 and delete the added §11.3 sentence.
The memo states the original §11.2 excluded gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP indemnity. It states the cap is 'the prior 12 months' fees'.
It states that Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 limit exclusivity to Series 7 Housings in the United States and uses this as the comparison baseline.

The header states New York governing law, and MSA §16 is referenced. The assumptions section expressly flags that New York and UCC points are general principles to be verified. No case citations are invented.
The memo is addressed to the partner and has a bottom line and an assumptions/facts-needed section. Issues are ranked by importance, each with Where / Why it matters / Fix / Facts needed.

The Term Sheet is used only as evidence of the deal and leverage, never as a document needing a fix. The 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not treated as defects; the 45-day point is only a calendaring reminder about the dispute notice.

Exclusivity is attributed to MSA §4.3, assignment to §15.2 and the cap change to Amendment §2, with correct party orientation. The statutory reference to UCC §2-305 is covered by the express verification flag. Minor slips, such as calling the IP indemnity 'cap-exempt' in the insurance bullet, do not materially misstate the documents.
